description:
Write ADR-0014's clause — the blocker the 2026-09-03 re-run left on KCB count (iii), and the one the ADR itself said would 'land with counts (ii) and (iii)'.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE TEXT (2026-09-12, before this tasklist was authored). ADR-0014's Decision section states four parts and says each is written 'so it can be implemented without consulting this record' — and none of them is in the spec. §7.3a requires 'an explicit deprecated marking on the predecessor' plus a removal version; §7.3d requires discovery to keep returning a deprecated entry 'marked, and carrying its removal version' while ranking it below any non-deprecated entry; §3's ranking bullet repeats the same obligation. NO FIELD CARRIES EITHER: §2's manifest example carries `version`, `schema_id`, `binding`, `cost`, `volume` and `effect` and no marking, and §3's `find` response shape — extended by MA-8 with `served_by`, `observed_at` and a result-level `incomplete[]` — names no deprecation field. The ADR's own amendment of 2026-09-03 records the walk confirming it from the other direction: 'no deprecation field exists on a §2 capability entry or in §3's response shape.'

WHY IT IS A BLOCKER AND NOT A TIDY-UP. §3.1(d)'s de-duplication converse merges two attributions that agree on provider KINP id, `(name, version)` and `schema_id`. A deprecation marking is none of those three — §7.1 step 1 drops every non-shape key, so the digest does not move; the predecessor's own entry gains the marking in place, so `version` does not move; and §7.2's table has no bump row for marking a capability deprecated. So a stale attribution and a deprecation-marked one satisfy the converse EXACTLY and MUST be returned as one entry whose marking is undefined, because the field is undefined — and §3.1(e) cannot fire, because the converse has just removed the visible disagreement.

THE FOUR PARTS, AS THE ADR STATES THEM: (1) the marking and its removal version are named fields on the §2 capability entry, carried through §3's `find` response — an extension of MA-8's shape, never a second envelope, optional on read and write, absent meaning NOT deprecated; (2) a registry MUST NOT synthesize a value for a field outside the merge key — where attributions disagree the merged entry carries each attribution's own copy bound to the `served_by` and `observed_at` that supplied it and MUST mark that they disagree; (3) where the disagreeing field is a gate, the restriction wins — any attribution marking the capability deprecated makes the merged entry deprecated for §7.3d's ranking, ADR-0013's monotone-restrictive discipline reused rather than a second convention invented; (4) none of it licenses reconciliation — §3.1(d)'s prohibition on silently picking between two AUTHORITIES is untouched, and parts 2 and 3 apply only within the converse.

ADDITIVE, AND BOUNDED. No verb, plane, port kind or authority role is added; a single-registry deployment emits none of it and is conformant unchanged; a consumer MUST ignore fields it does not understand (§7.2). What the ADR deliberately does NOT decide stays undecided: no wall-clock timestamp on the marking (DEFER-E unmoved), no cadence or TTL on a discovery binding (DEFER-D unmoved), no bump row for `volume` or `effect` (a separate §7.2 change, and a separate tasklist), and no peering topology, membership or trust weighting.

WHAT IT CLOSES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. Count (iii) does not close until the Steps 5-7 re-run walks clean against the folded text, and clearing it still leaves KCB's other FOUR counts open — so this promotes nothing on its own. Say that in the record rather than leaving a reader to re-derive it.

userStories.title: Parts 2-4 — no synthesis, the restriction wins, and no reconciliation licensed
userStories.description: The merge rule itself, on §3.1(d)'s converse. Three clauses, each stated so an implementer needs neither the ADR nor this tasklist to get it right.
acceptanceCriteria: A registry MUST NOT synthesize a value for a field outside the merge key. Where attributions disagree on such a field, the merged entry carries EACH attribution's own copy bound to the `served_by` and `observed_at` that supplied it, and MUST mark that the attributions disagree — which is what §3.1(e) needs in order to fire, and what keeps §3.1(a) intact.

Where the disagreeing field is a gate, the restriction wins: if ANY attribution marks the capability deprecated, the merged entry is deprecated for the purposes of §7.3d's ranking and marking. The clause cites ADR-0013's monotone-restrictive discipline as reused, and states the measured asymmetry that justifies it (a false deprecation costs a ranking demotion on an entry §7.3d keeps returning and keeps functional; a missed one is the silent case §7.2 makes non-recoverable).

The clause says explicitly that it licenses NO reconciliation: two entries from two AUTHORITIES naming the same capability are still both returned and still never silently picked between; parts 2 and 3 apply only WITHIN the converse — one provider, one `(name, version)`, one `schema_id`, reached more than once.

What ADR-0014 leaves undecided is left undecided and said so in the text or in the fold record: no wall-clock timestamp (DEFER-E unmoved), no cadence or TTL on a discovery binding (DEFER-D unmoved), no §7.2 bump row for `volume` or `effect`, no peering topology or trust weighting.

The KCB version move is decided under §7.2's own table and recorded with its reasoning, and the two declared removals riding on KCB's minor axis are checked rather than tripped: §2.3's legacy extension-URI namespace root is declared removed at KCB 0.6.0 and KMI's `application/vnd.koine.edl+json` at KMI 0.4.0. If the version moves, all three status mirrors (`README.md`, `specs/README.md`, `ECOSYSTEM.md`) move with it — `check-doc-integrity.mjs` enforces that.
GATES: koine's six checks green, with observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: Parts 2-4 landed on §3.1(d)'s converse as *Merging attributions merges attributions, never contents*: (i) MUST NOT synthesize a field outside the merge key — on disagreement the merged entry carries each attribution's own copy bound to its `served_by`/`observed_at`, the per-attribution form being the machine-readable mark of disagreement (what §3.1(e) needs to fire; keeps §3.1(a) intact); (ii) where the field is a gate the restriction wins — any attribution marking `deprecated` makes the merged entry deprecated for §7.3d's ranking, ADR-0013's monotone-restrictive discipline cited as reused, with the measured asymmetry stated (false deprecation = a ranking demotion on an entry §7.3d keeps returning and keeps functional, corrected by one re-read; missed = §7.2's non-recoverable silent case); it deliberately does NOT reach `removal_version` (a planning datum — §7.3e forbids shortening a window, so taking the earliest of two reads would be the registry doing exactly that); (iii) no reconciliation licensed — two AUTHORITIES still both returned, never silently picked between, (i)/(ii) apply only WITHIN the converse. A closing paragraph leaves undecided what ADR-0014 leaves undecided: DEFER-E unmoved (no wall-clock), DEFER-D unmoved (no cadence/TTL), no §7.2 bump row for `volume`/`effect` (BP-8/AP-9 stay open), no peering topology/membership/trust weighting. VERSION: KCB 0.5.0 -> 0.5.1, PATCH, decided and reasoned in the changelog + status note — every field optional on read and write, §7.2's table undisturbed, no published `schema_id` moves, and the bump is deliberately NOT declared under §7.2's table (it governs a published capability, has no row for a manifest field outside the digest, and declaring a spec bump under it is the BP-8/AP-9 defect). Declared removals CHECKED not tripped: KCB 0.6.0 stays spoken for by §2.3's legacy extension-URI-root removal (window runs TO 0.6.0), and KMI's `application/vnd.koine.edl+json` rides KMI 0.4.0, a different spec's axis. All three status mirrors moved with the header (README.md:63, specs/README.md:17, ECOSYSTEM.md:48) plus specs/README.md:288's 'all six sit there now' prose and CLAUDE.md's Current state bullet. GATES all six green as observed: doc-integrity OK (61 files, 1709 relative links, 3 status tables match, capability-bus 0.5.1 candidate); doc-links 0 dead references (0 distinct targets); schemas OK (9 schemas, 278 positions, 80 $refs, 3 fixtures); registry OK (31 relation names); tasklist-categories OK (9 categorized); roadmap coverage OK (53 completed) / stale OK (43 merged) / park OK.

userStories.title: Re-run e2e-multi-authority Steps 5-7 against the folded text, and record what still blocks KCB
userStories.description: Count (iii) does not close until the re-run walks clean. Walk the prose — an encoding's exit code is not the verdict (DR-8 records `kcs:multi-authority` returning green over six blocking deltas).
acceptanceCriteria: `scenarios/e2e-multi-authority.md` Steps 5-7 are re-run BY HAND against the folded text, with a per-step verdict recorded in the scenario's own re-run section. Step 5 is the one that broke on this clause, so it is the step the walk must answer.
The walk is against the PROSE, not a replay: DR-8 records this scenario's own encoding returning `green` over six blocking deltas, so a green encoding is not evidence here.
The verdict is recorded honestly, including a NOT-clean one and any new delta it returns. Count (iii) closes only on a clean walk.

The record states that KCB's other FOUR counts stay open regardless of this verdict, so this tasklist promotes nothing on its own; `docs/reference/promotability.md` is updated to match what this walk changed.
ADR-0014 gains a short amendment recording that its clause landed and where, so the ADR does not keep reading as decided-but-unwritten.
